title: arXiv Trending Biology and Biomedicine — Daily, 2026-11-17
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred relevance ranking from an incomplete biomedical corpus, not a popularity ranking.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: The latest batch available today is dated 17 November 2026. Its configured category listings show 43 appearances, deduplicated to 40 arXiv IDs; 10 notable papers are selected below. The strongest recurring pattern is computational methods tied to biological measurements: antibody engineering and assay interpretation, transcriptome prediction, and spatial multi-omics. Spoken agenda: what the antibody campaigns learned about measuring molecules, where transcriptome models generalize, and what spatial omics methods still need.
sections.global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred relevance ranking from an incomplete biomedical corpus, not a popularity ranking.

sections.title: Reasoning in the loop: antibody lead optimization by probing mechanism and measurement
sections.abstract: Two antibody lead-optimization campaigns combine human researchers, a general-purpose AI agent, and assay-specific biophysical reasoning to improve leads while revising misleading thermal metrics.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improved affinity and stability for an anti-albumin VHH and an anti-mesothelin scFv after reinterpreting scaffold-specific thermal assay signals.
sections.unique_caveat: The leads' key measurements rely on one or two replicates; the authors call for confirmation, higher-sensitivity affinity measurements, and further aggregation and stress testing.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Strong direct fit to protein engineering; the authors report two assay campaigns, seven rounds and about 1,010 variants, with perturbation tests of revised measurements.

sections.title: In-context learning predicts clinical endpoints from bulk transcriptomes across diseases and platforms
sections.abstract: PRTS uses labelled cohort examples as context to predict clinical or phenotypic outcomes from bulk RNA profiles without per-cohort training.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a small mean-accuracy lead over their strongest pre-specified comparator, driven mainly by within-cohort prediction and TCGA survival tasks.
sections.unique_caveat: Across cohorts and unseen sites the model is level with the strongest comparator; retrospective benchmark results do not establish prospective clinical utility. The paper also documents a correction to earlier comparator gene selection.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Strong RNA/translational relevance; the paper evaluates 175 held-out RealBulk tasks and 44 TCGA tasks, and reports a 220-million-parameter model trained on six million generated tasks.

sections.title: multiCAsp: Spatially Informed Canonical Association Analysis of Multi-Omic Data
sections.abstract: multiCAsp integrates spatially resolved molecular modalities by imposing a graph-Laplacian prior on shared latent factors.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report stronger latent-factor and loading recovery in their tested simulations, plus spatially coherent factors and cross-modal prediction in the two real datasets.
sections.unique_caveat: Real-data demonstrations cover only two datasets; dense loadings, factor-dimension choices, and modality-specific PCA truncation complicate interpretation and generalization.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct multi-omics relevance; authors compare against three methods in simulations and analyze macaque cortex metabolomics/proteomics and human renal-carcinoma gene/protein data.

sections.title: Multi-Assay Antibody Developability Prediction with Shared Structure-Language Representations
sections.abstract: MADM combines per-residue structural descriptors, protein-language-model embeddings, and multi-assay training to predict antibody developability measurements.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that combining structural and sequence representations gives modest accuracy gains, while multi-assay training helps on correlated assays.
sections.unique_caveat: Performance falls on the 80-antibody GDPa3 hold-out, and assay/source-specific measurement calibration can be entangled with sequence generalization.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct biochemistry relevance and cross-listing; the authors report evaluation across eight assays built from 29 open data sources, plus separate antibody panels.

sections.title: From Mutation to Medication: Characterizing Failures of Clinical LLMs to Respect Genomic Resistance
sections.abstract: The authors audit whether language models endorse cancer therapies despite curated genomic evidence of resistance.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that apparent resistance failures vary by evidence strength and source, and that supplying correct curated evidence reduced unqualified strong recommendations in an oracle-style test.
sections.unique_caveat: Matched-group analysis is described as exploratory and was specified after the pre-registered analysis; curated cases and oracle-provided evidence do not reproduce real clinical retrieval or decision workflows.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Strong genomics/oncology relevance; the study tests ten models against 1,464 curated resistance cases drawn from five knowledge bases.

sections.title: From the possible to the optimal: differentiable optimization of gene regulatory networks
sections.abstract: jaxgrn combines differentiable programming and stochastic simulation to optimize gene-regulatory networks against biological-function constraints.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report recurring optimal network regimes as constraints on pattern formation and positional information change.
sections.unique_caveat: Findings are from mathematical modeling and stochastic simulations, not experiments demonstrating that the inferred architectures occur in embryos.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct molecular-network relevance and cross-listing; the authors describe GPU optimization of thousands of networks in embryonic-patterning case studies.

sections.title: Calpha: Toward Native Biomolecular Intelligence in a General-Purpose Language Model
sections.abstract: Calpha routes a language model's residue representations into a pretrained structure head to generate single-chain protein structures.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors show a general-purpose LLM can emit single-chain structures from its own residue states, while explicitly leaving complex prediction and structure understanding for future work.
sections.unique_caveat: Comparisons differ in trainable weights, training duration, and crop length; the paper reports lower scores for longer chains and reduced accuracy on its evaluated language benchmark subset.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Protein-structure relevance; the authors report TM-score evaluations on FoldBench-334, CASP16 domains, and a CAMEO-style PDB set.

sections.title: Arginine metabolism drives tumor immune escape by shaping an immunosuppressive microenvironment
sections.abstract: A calibrated mathematical model examines how arginine metabolism and macrophage polarization may shape tumor-immune dynamics.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors' simulations predict tumor-growth effects of arginine administration and possible synergy between arginine depletion and checkpoint blockade.
sections.unique_caveat: These are model-based predictions, not reported intervention experiments or evidence of treatment benefit in animals or people.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct molecular-medicine relevance; the model is calibrated against tumor-growth data from three mouse cohorts.

sections.title: Beyond AUC: Do Mammography Risk Models Predict When Cancer Occurs?
sections.abstract: The paper tests whether longitudinal mammography risk metrics capture time-to-diagnosis and proposes a two-stage model separating whether from when cancer occurs.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that a proposed two-stage model matches LMV-Net's discrimination while improving the ranking of cancer cases by time to diagnosis in this evaluation.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a retrospective dataset analysis; timing performance and generalization require validation on independent cohorts and clinical settings.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct biomedical-imaging relevance and cross-listing; the authors re-evaluate two models on a five-year CSAW-CC setting using timing-specific metrics.

sections.title: Scaling large language model-assisted line-of-therapy adjudication with human-in-the-loop evidence-calibrated selection
sections.abstract: Evidence-calibrated selection prioritizes oncology treatment histories for clinician review while feeding confirmed adjudications back into model-assisted line-of-therapy assignment.
sections.claimed_contribution: In the reported simulation, reviewing 44.6% of patients yielded 5% residual error, versus 62.2% for LLM-confidence-directed review and 81.9% for random review.
sections.unique_caveat: Results are simulation-based on a small, study-specific adjudicated set; operational reliability across institutions and cancer types remains untested.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Oncology data-methods relevance; the authors report simulations based on 136 clinician-adjudicated multiple-myeloma patients.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.content: Protein engineering, representation and assay interpretation (#1, #4, #7): Two antibody papers make measurement quality and assay transfer central, while Calpha tests a language-model route to single-chain structure generation; these are distinct contributions, not independent validation. Learning from molecular data for biomedical tasks (#2, #5, #10): bulk RNA prediction, genomic-resistance auditing, and treatment-history adjudication pair machine-learning systems with biomedical evidence, but use different evaluation designs. Spatial and regulatory systems modeling (#3, #6, #8): spatial multi-omics, optimized gene-regulatory networks, and tumor-metabolism dynamics connect quantitative models to tissue or cell-state questions; only #3 tests its method on measured tissue datasets, while #6 and #8 are computational models. Measurement-aware risk evaluation (#9, #1): these ask whether measurements capture the intended biological or clinical property in different retrospective or in-vitro settings.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.content: Confirm antibody leads and assay proxies (#1): replicate the leads; use longer-window BLI or higher-sensitivity SPR; test aggregation with isothermal holds and size-exclusion measurements; extend with stress testing and mammalian expression. Test transcriptome-model transport (#2): evaluate prospective or independently curated cohorts with site-held-out splits and pre-specified comparisons across platforms and endpoints. Improve spatial-omics interpretation (#3): test sparse loadings, quantify factor-selection uncertainty, and validate on additional tissues, resolutions, and matched three-or-more-modality data. Stress-test oncology evidence handling (#5, #10): use independent knowledge bases, incomplete or conflicting evidence, and multi-site clinician-reviewed histories.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: This batch is strongest in methods that make molecular measurements more usable: antibody engineering, bulk-transcriptome prediction, and spatial multi-omics. The leading results remain bounded by small assay replication, retrospective or simulated evaluation, and unresolved cross-site generalization. Treat the list as a relevance-focused snapshot of arXiv, not a signal of clinical readiness or field-wide popularity.
